title: Sony Music Sues Kroger in Latest Lawsuit Over Songs on Social Media: ‘Rampant Infringement’
summary: The label claims the grocery chain used music by Beyoncé, Billy Joel, Michael Jackson and Outkast in social media advertisements — the latest in a flood of such cases.
contentText:
Sony Music is suing Kroger over accusations that the supermarket giant used songs by Harry Styles , Mariah Carey , Miley Cyrus and SZA without permission in TikTok and Instagram posts.

The case is the latest in a blitz of litigation from major labels over music used by commercial brands in social media posts. Marriott, Chili’s and NBA teams have all faced lawsuits, and many more companies have settled privately.

In a complaint filed Friday (Aug. 21), Sony claims Kroger — a grocery behemoth with 2,800 stores across 35 states — has posted nearly 400 unauthorized uses of its music, including songs by Beyoncé , Billy Joel , Michael Jackson , Outkast , Prince , Pitbull and The White Stripes .

In Friday’s lawsuit, Sony accused Kroger of flouting those rules to “capitalize on the popularity, artistry, and entertainment value” of its music.

“The Sony music recordings are central to the effectiveness and appeal of the videos,” the company’s lawyers write. “[The music] enables the Kroger parties to take advantage of the social media platforms’ algorithms and reach users who do not necessarily follow [them].”

The lawsuit lists numerous specific examples of Kroger’s posts, including an Instagram post advertising watermelons set to Styles’ “Watermelon Sugar” and another promoting holiday cocktail recipes to Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You.”

“[Kroger’s] selection of the [songs] is calculated: The Kroger Parties choose specific recordings because of their cultural and seasonal associations and use those associations to sell products,” Sony’s lawyers write. “These are precisely the types of uses for which Sony Music charges a license fee.”

Numerous songs were allegedly used when they were trending hits, including Cyrus’ “Flowers,” Doja Cat ‘s “Paint The Town Red” and Beyoncé’s “Texas Hold ‘Em” when each song was at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 .

A spokeswoman for Kroger did not immediately return a request for comment on Monday (Aug. 24).
